We have reported multiple times on the use of Apple Vision Pro in the medical sector. This week, Stryker announced the completion of the first surgery performed using an innovative application on the Vision Pro.

The surgery was a hip arthroscopy performed using the SportSuite Vision application, which can bring "critical digital content into the surgeon's virtual space." Content includes arthroscopic images, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images.

The following is Stryker's description of the application:

SportSuite Vision brings critical digital content into the surgeon's visual space, allowing them to observe physical objects in the operating room while using digital tools such as arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images. When performing arthroscopic surgery, surgeons often need to rely on multiple displays positioned at various locations in the operating room to access imaging and surgical data. By integrating multiple data sources into the surgeon's field of view, this technology can reduce reliance on traditional displays and support a smoother, more ergonomic surgical workflow.

SportSuite Vision received FDA De Novo authorisation on 17 July. Stryker stated that the application is the first to receive FDA authorisation for use with the Vision Pro during surgery.

In addition, Pfizer also announced this week that it is using the Apple Vision Pro to "create memorable immersive experiences" to "showcase" its determination to "conquer cancer."

For more information about the experience, please visit the Groove Jones website.
